title: The capacity band does not hold the charge between the BMS stops
found: On 200 synthetic packs the monthly 90 % band held the charge between the stops at the date in 1524 of 4782 month ends (32 %); the estimate reads +0.63 points of nominal capacity above it on average. Against the capacity between the rest voltages it reports, the band held 3789 of 4562 (83 %), +0.12 points on average; that truth was chosen after the first results.

title: Apparent charge loss (A4) is biased on synthetic packs
found: The band held the true drain in 182 of 200 packs (91 %). The estimate is off by -0.08 mA on average (standard deviation 0.17 mA) on a true drain of 50 mA, just outside ±0.02 (2 sd/√200): a small bias remains. Release 0.1.0: the band held 87 of 200; +4.43 mA on average (standard deviation 2.34 mA); 194 of 200 packs read above the truth.

title: Storage at a middle state of charge gets a wrong capacity without the pack's voltage limits
found: Do not use the capacity (A1) on storage that works at a middle state of charge unless the pack's documented voltage limits are given (`PackSpec.voltage_max_v`, `voltage_min_v`). With them, version 0.3 refuses: on simulated packs cycled daily between 25 and 75 % and never charged full, 200 of 200 packs with 0 estimated month ends and every reason 'not possible from this data', for NMC, LFP and the string. Without them it still takes the edges of the daily window for full and empty and reports a median 51.8 % (NMC), 51.0 % (LFP), 51.0 % (the string) of the true capacity, with the status `estimated` and the label "full and empty are the ends of the observed window; not checked against voltage limits".

title: Apparent charge loss (A4) trails a new leak
found: On simulated packs with a cell leak the A4 band holds the true apparent charge loss at 3424 of 3549 (96.5%) month ends without a leak, 1869 of 3574 (52.3%) at 5 mA and 1033 of 3590 (28.8%) at 15 mA, before the onset and from 180 days after it. Version 0.3's band is narrower; the estimate weighs its history with a 180-day memory, so after a new leak it trails the change and the band no longer covers it.

title: The fade rate's band is too narrow on synthetic packs
found: On 200 synthetic packs the band of the fade rate held the true usable fade (-1.88) in 27.0% (rule 85-95 %: fail). The reading times move the rate's bias, the quadratic terms narrow its band; together the band is too narrow for the bias.
